key_insight: Odd stiffness survives in 3D strain-gradient continua even at full isotropy, but non-Hermitian elastodynamics requires anisotropy.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports homogenization and design of active, nonreciprocal metamaterials with internal length scales and tunable elastic-wave amplification or attenuation.
method: Classify fourth-, fifth-, and sixth-order odd stiffness tensors across 3D point-group symmetries.
Use dynamic virtual work to derive equilibrium equations, higher-order boundary conditions, and the generalized acoustic tensor.
Numerically analyze wave dispersion in a transversely hemitropic odd elastic continuum.
evidence_signal: Analytical symmetry results establish Hermitian acoustic tensors in isotropic and hemitropic limits, while numerical analysis of a transversely hemitropic case reveals exceptional points and simultaneous wave-component amplification and attenuation.
watch_item: The abstract reports theoretical and numerical results, not experimental validation or a demonstrated microstructure realizing the required anisotropic odd moduli.
paper_title: Odd Elasticity in Strain-Gradient Continua: Anisotropy Classification and Non-Hermitian Elastodynamics
